# Error codes

Every failure has a `code` and a `category`; the exit code depends on the category only, and `0` is success. `error.retryable` tells whether the same call may succeed later.

## What to do

| Error category | Exit | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid` | 1 | The input breaks the ontology or a rule. Read `error.details.findings`, fix the values and retry with `--dry-run` first. |
| `not_found` | 1 | The graph, entity or term does not exist. Check the reference; `error.details` may list close matches. |
| `refused` | 1 | The request cannot be carried out as given (an ambiguous reference, a change set too large or with broken local references, a graph that is archived, read-only or outside the project). Change the request; do not repeat it. |
| `usage` | 2 | The command line is wrong or incomplete (for example no graph selected). Check the command in `references/commands.md` or `graph describe commands --json`. |
| `denied` | 3 | You are not permitted. Stop and tell the user; do not retry under another identity and do not work around it. `graph whoami --json` shows what you may do. If a reason is required, retry with `--reason`. If the batch is too large, split it into documents of at most `max_batch` operations and tell the user that it is no longer one transaction. |
| `conflict` | 4 | Someone else changed the data or the key was used for another request. Read the entity again, then decide whether to retry. |
| `unavailable` | 5 | Storage, the audit log, a lock or the installation is not usable. If `error.retryable` is true, retry later with the same `--idempotency-key`; otherwise tell the user, a maintainer has to look at it. |
| `internal` | 6 | A bug in the CLI. Report the full envelope to the user. |

## When graph talks to a server

- `remote.unreachable`, `remote.unauthorized`: stop and tell the user. Never look for, set or pass a token yourself.
- `remote.outcome_unknown`: a write was sent and its answer lost. Run exactly the command in `hint` (the same write with the same idempotency key, safe to repeat), never a changed one, then read the result.
- `access.project_mismatch`: the token belongs to another project. Stop and tell the user; never change the project.
- `remote.client_outdated`: this program is not the build the server runs. Stop and tell the user the command in `hint`, which installs the server's build and refreshes the skills; never install or change the program yourself.
- `remote.version_differs` (a warning): the server runs another build. With `details.compatible: true` the commands and this skill are the same: finish the task, then tell the user once that `graph self update` installs the server's build.

## When an installed skill is outdated

- `skills.outdated`: this skill, or the skill of the graph, was installed for an older program or an older state of the graph, so the write was refused. Stop and tell the user the command in `hint`, which refreshes the installed skills; never change skill files yourself. After the refresh, read the skills again before repeating the write.
- `skills.stale` (a warning on a read): the same, but the answer is right. Finish the read and tell the user.

## When a retract or supersede is refused

- `data.referential.target_referenced` (in `error.details.findings` of `write.invalid`): active entities still point at the entity over a relation that keeps its targets active; `actual.sources` lists them (at most 20 of `actual.count`). Decide for each: relink it (on a supersede, to the replacing entity) or retract it when it is withdrawn too; ask the user when it is not clear. Then put those writes and the refused one into one `graph apply` change set and dry-run it. Never retract an entity only to get the write through.
- The same code as a warning in `data.findings`: the write went through; tell the user which entities still point at the entity.

## When a relation does not fit the types

- `data.referential.domain_violation` and `data.referential.range_violation` (in `error.details.findings` of `write.invalid`): the relation does not accept the type of the source or of the target. Do not retry the same edge. The finding's `connecting` names what the model accepts between the two types: `direct` lists relations (`from` -relation-> `to`), and when there are none `paths` lists up to three chains of two relations over an intermediate entity. Pick one; a path means creating or finding the intermediate entity and writing both edges in one `graph apply` change set, dry-run first. When both lists are empty the model has no such connection: ask the user.
